newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: CENSUS RESULTS PROVE AUSTRALIA'S POPULATION IS AGEING
Data released today from the 1996 census confirms Australia's population is ageing.
The information from the final census this century is now publicly available.
The 1996 census counted nearly 17.9 million people in Australia, a growth of more than 6 per cent in five years.
Australia's population is ageing with a median age of 34 years compared to 32 in 1991.

The number of people of indigenous origin increased by a third to 2 percent of the total population, the rise partly explained by people's increased willingness to declare their indigenous background.
Of those born overseas, more than a third were from the United Kingdom, Ireland or New Zealand.
Of the remainder, the highest numbers came from Italy, Vietnam, China and Germany.
SECOND AUSTRALIAN DIES FOLLOWING ISRAELI BRIDGE COLLAPSE
A second Australian has died of injuries received after a bridge collapsed before the opening of the world Jewish community's major sports event, the Maccabia Games, in Israel.
More than 50 people were hurt in the collapse, several of them seriously, sparking angry claims about poor safety standards.
The dead and injured, all Australians, were plunged into a shallow, muddy river, after the bridge cracked and gave way.
It had been constructed especially to ensure the 5,500 athletes attending the Games could cross the river to enter the Ramat Gan Stadium for the opening ceremony.
But the bridge failed to support even a few hundred athletes.
Israel's Police Minister, Avigdor Kahalani, said the construction had received all the right permits, yet it still collapsed.
Police are now preparing to speak to those who built the bridge, as survivors express anger that lax safety standards have so marred a much anticipated sporting event.
Media officer with the Australian team, Peter Scott, says a decision will be made later today whether to continue Australia's participation in the competition.
Mr Scott: "A team meeting will be held, where a decision will be made. That is not to suggest in anyway that we are withdrawing, but it is just to say that we simply haven't decided."
AUSTRALIA SUSPENDS MILITARY AID TO CAMBODIA
Australia has suspended its military aid to Cambodia, worth about $2 million.
Federal Cabinet has discussed Australia's foreign aid program to Cambodia, in the wake of the coup by second Prime Minister, Hun Sen.
Cambodia's Ambassador to Canberra, Chheang Vun, met Australia's Foreign Minister Alexander Downer this afternoon.
Mr Chheang says Australia is to suspend and review its military aid to Cambodia, but will not cut or suspend the broader aid program, worth about $30 million a year.
He says Mr Downer also reinforced Australia's call for peace and stability in Cambodia, and for next year's elections to be free and fair as scheduled.
Mr Downer is expected to make a statement this afternoon.
SYDNEY HOTELS GAIN MULTI-MILLION DOLLAR INDUCEMENT
The owners of Sydney hotels have been given a multi-million dollar inducement to provide rooms to the Olympic Organising Committee.
This is on top of the $35 million contribution from the State Government over the next two years.
Sydney's Olympic Organisers will halve their commission to 5 percent if hotels agree to contracts by the end of the year.
A phasing in of the bed tax will also be available, but only for those hotels that agree to provide room space.
Calls from cruise lines that they be exempted from the tax have been successful.
The international body representing cruise ship companies had threatened a boycott of Sydney during the Games, which would have created a problem for the Olympic Organisers.
The Australian Hotel Association has recommitted to reserving 80 percent of rooms to cover Olympic obligations.
It now appears the $600 million worth of sponsorship deal threatened by the impasse is safe, and new contracts can be signed with confidence.
SMITH FAMILY REJECTS JOB LOSS/REGIONAL CLAIMS
The Sydney-based management of the Smith Family has rejected claims that a re-structure of the organisation will lead to job losses and the closure of regional outlets.
It has been claimed by people within the Smith Family, that nine regional outlets will be closed, and 11 managers have been told their jobs are redundant.
But Manager of Sales and Marketing, Ulysses Chioatto, says while the 11 managers will be made redundant, they will be given opportunities to apply for other jobs in the organisation.
Mr Chioatto says none of the regional outlets will be closed or scaled down.
He says the claims have been made to tarnish the name of the Smith Family.
GLOWEAVE CLOSES LAST AUSTRALIAN FACTORY
One of Australia's best-known retail brand names says it is another victim of reduced protection, under successive Federal Governments.
Business-shirt maker, Gloweave, is closing its last remaining Australian factory, employing 80 people, in the inner-Melbourne suburb of Fitzroy.
This could leave Gloweave as an all-imported product.
Managing Director, David Same, says he hopes the Federal Government will not implement an Industry Commission recommendation to cut tariff protection for clothing from 34 per cent to 5 per cent.
Mr Same says 90,000 jobs are at stake.
He says former Minister John Button, whom he says was the architect of the winding-down of protection, would probably now say it was a mistake.
Mr Same: "I don't know which way the Government will go now. Given that they've shown some kind of common sense with the car industry, I'd expect the same with the rag trade."
INJUNCTION ISSUED AGAINST FOSSEY'S OVER PRICE-FIXING
The Federal Court has acted to stop price-fixing of soft-drinks, by a Brisbane branch of the Fossey's department store.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission received complaints last year, made against the store in the Queens Street Mall.
It was alleged the store had stopped a small business licensee from selling cans of soft-drink from a take-away outlet in the store, unless they were sold at a certain price.
The court today issued an injunction against Fossey's.
The ACCC says Fossey's new manager, Target, has now responded to concerns over what is believed to have been an isolated action by one store manager.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
